name: spring-security-hardening
description: "Spring Security 6 hardening for Spring Boot APIs and services: SecurityFilterChain with lambda DSL, OAuth2 Resource Server JWT with issuer/audience validation, method security, CSRF, CORS, password encoding, Actuator protection, security headers, and secret management. Use it for every security configuration or protected endpoint."

# Skill: Spring Security 6 Hardening

## Implementation Rules:
- **[FORBIDDEN]** Do not use `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` (removed in Spring Security 6), `@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity` (replaced by `@EnableMethodSecurity`), or the chained syntax with `.and()` (deprecated in 6.1 and removed in Spring Security 7 / Spring Boot 4).
- **[MANDATORY]** Define security with one or more `SecurityFilterChain` beans built with the lambda DSL (`http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> ...)`), in a dedicated `@Configuration` + `@EnableWebSecurity` class; with multiple chains use explicit `securityMatcher(...)` and `@Order`, and always keep a final catch-all chain without `securityMatcher`, because requests not intercepted by any chain do not go through Spring Security.
- **[SECURITY]** Apply deny-by-default: explicitly list public endpoints with `requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/api/v1/catalog/**").permitAll()` and always close with `anyRequest().denyAll()` (or `authenticated()` only if every authenticated endpoint is also protected at the method level).
- **[PATTERN]** Configure APIs as an OAuth2 JWT Resource Server with `oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()))` and `spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri`; do not implement custom JWT filters with manual token parsing.
- **[SECURITY]** Always validate the JWT's issuer and audience: use `spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.audiences` (Spring Boot 3.2+) or a `JwtDecoder` with a `DelegatingOAuth2TokenValidator` that combines `JwtValidators.createDefaultWithIssuer(issuer)` and `new JwtClaimValidator<List<String>>("aud", aud -> aud != null && aud.contains("orders-api"))`; restrict algorithms with `jws-algorithms: RS256`.
- **[PATTERN]** Map roles and scopes with a `JwtAuthenticationConverter` and `JwtGrantedAuthoritiesConverter` (`setAuthoritiesClaimName("roles")`, `setAuthorityPrefix("ROLE_")`) or with the `authorities-claim-name`/`authority-prefix` properties (Spring Boot 3.2+), without mapping logic scattered across controllers.
- **[MANDATORY]** Enable `@EnableMethodSecurity` and protect every sensitive use case with `@PreAuthorize` (e.g. `@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('SCOPE_orders:write')")`); for ownership rules delegate to a bean (`@PreAuthorize("@orderAccess.isOwner(#orderId, authentication)")`) instead of chaining complex SpEL expressions.
- **[SECURITY]** Disable CSRF only for stateless APIs with bearer tokens, together with `sessionManagement(s -> s.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS))`; for applications with sessions and cookies keep CSRF enabled with `CookieCsrfTokenRepository.withHttpOnlyFalse()` for SPAs.
- **[SECURITY]** Configure CORS explicitly with `cors(c -> c.configurationSource(source))` and a `CorsConfiguration` with listed origins, methods, and headers (`setAllowedOrigins(List.of("https://app.acme.com"))`); `allowedOrigins("*")` together with `allowCredentials(true)` is forbidden, and so is `@CrossOrigin` scattered on controllers.
- **[SECURITY]** Encode passwords with `PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder()` (prefix `{bcrypt}`, `{argon2}`) or `Argon2PasswordEncoder.defaultsForSpringSecurity_v5_8()` (requires BouncyCastle); `NoOpPasswordEncoder`, `MessageDigest` MD5/SHA-1, and unsalted hashes are forbidden.
- **[SECURITY]** Protect Actuator with a dedicated `SecurityFilterChain` (`securityMatcher(EndpointRequest.toAnyEndpoint())`, `@Order(1)`): `EndpointRequest.to(HealthEndpoint.class)` public, everything else `hasRole("OPS")`; prefer a separate `management.server.port` not exposed by the ingress.
- **[SECURITY]** Set the security headers: `headers(h -> h.contentSecurityPolicy(csp -> csp.policyDirectives("default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'")).frameOptions(f -> f.deny()).httpStrictTransportSecurity(hsts -> hsts.includeSubDomains(true).maxAgeInSeconds(31536000)).referrerPolicy(r -> r.policy(ReferrerPolicy.NO_REFERRER)))`.
- **[FORBIDDEN]** No secrets (client secrets, DB passwords, signing keys, API keys) in code or in versioned `application*.yml`: use environment variables (`${DB_PASSWORD}`), `spring.config.import=optional:configtree:/run/secrets/`, or Spring Cloud Vault (`spring.config.import=vault://`).
- **[SECURITY]** Do not expose internal details in errors: keep `server.error.include-stacktrace=never` and `server.error.include-message=never`, return `401`/`403` as `ProblemDetail` without revealing whether a resource exists, and never log `Authorization` headers, tokens, or passwords.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** Customize authentication/authorization error responses via `exceptionHandling(e -> e.authenticationEntryPoint(...).accessDeniedHandler(...))` or `BearerTokenAuthenticationEntryPoint`/`BearerTokenAccessDeniedHandler` for OAuth2 APIs, returning the correct `WWW-Authenticate` header.
- **[PATTERN]** Obtain the current user with `@AuthenticationPrincipal Jwt jwt` or `@CurrentSecurityContext` in web adapters and pass only a value object (`CustomerId`) to the domain, never the `Authentication` object.
- **[CONFIGURATION]** For compatibility with Spring Security 7 / Spring Boot 4 use `requestMatchers(String...)` or `PathPatternRequestMatcher` (6.5+) instead of the deprecated `AntPathRequestMatcher`/`MvcRequestMatcher`.
- **[TESTING]** Test the access matrix with `spring-security-test`: for every endpoint verify `401` without a token, `403` with insufficient authority, and `2xx` with `SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.jwt().authorities(new SimpleGrantedAuthority("SCOPE_orders:write"))`; test `@PreAuthorize` methods with `@WithMockUser`.
- **[TESTING]** Include dependency scanning in the pipeline (`org.owasp:dependency-check-maven` or Dependabot/Renovate) with a failure threshold of `failBuildOnCVSS=7`.
- **[REFERENCE]** See `EXAMPLES.md` in this folder for reference anti-patterns and best practices.
